title: Your Bookkeeper Isn't Going Anywhere: What Changes When a Fractional CFO Joins Too
linkedin:
Most owners who look at bringing in a fractional CFO get stuck on the same quiet worry before they even get to the decision.

It isn't the fee. It's the conversation they imagine having with the person who already does their books.

Does this mean telling my bookkeeper their work wasn't good enough?

We hear this often enough that it's worth naming directly, especially during Australian Small Business Month, when a lot of owner-led businesses are taking stock of how things are actually structured behind the scenes.

Here's the straightforward answer: a bookkeeper and a fractional CFO work at two different heights in the business, not on top of each other.

A bookkeeper keeps the ledger accurate, reconciled and compliant. That's precise, essential work. A fractional CFO takes that same clean ledger and turns it into a forward-looking read, used to decide whether to hire, hold off on a price rise, or chase a slow-paying customer harder.

Neither role is the junior version of the other.

In practice, almost nothing changes about how the bookkeeping gets done day to day. What changes is what happens to the numbers after they leave that layer, and often the role actually gets easier, not smaller. Owners stop routing commercial questions to the person whose job was never to answer them.

The honest move is naming this early with whoever already handles the books, rather than letting them hear about it secondhand. A short, plain conversation about what stays the same tends to settle the worry faster than any amount of reassurance after the fact.

A question we hear often from business owners across Brisbane, the Gold Coast, and up and down the East Coast: if I bring in extra financial support, what happens to the person who already does my books?

It's a fair thing to wonder about, and worth answering plainly. A bookkeeper or BAS agent keeps your financial records accurate, reconciled, and compliant. That work doesn't change and it doesn't go anywhere. What a fractional CFO adds is a different layer on top, taking those same numbers and using them to answer forward-looking questions, like whether now is the time to hire, adjust pricing, or hold off on a purchase.

In practice, most bookkeepers find the role gets easier once this layer is in place, because the commercial questions that used to land on their desk finally go to the person whose job it is to answer them.

If you've been putting off a conversation about financial support because you weren't sure how it would affect your existing team, this month's piece on the ProfitPulse blog works through exactly that. Read the full piece on the blog.
